title: Koki (Gâteau de cornille)
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik.com)
desc: White beans soaked overnight, skinned, crushed with chilli and mixed with palm oil and water to a smooth, fairly liquid batter, tied in banana leaves and cooked 4 hours in a leaf-lined pot.
longDesc: The Afrik printing calls koki a ‘gâteau de cornille’ of Cameroonian origin from the Mbo culture (known as moin-moin in Nigeria). The white beans are soaked the evening before, then rubbed against each other next day to remove the white skin. A thick-bottomed pot is lined with banana leaves (central rib removed) and 1 litre of water. The palm oil is warmed until lukewarm; the beans are crushed with the chilli, mixed with half the oil and, once absorbed, the rest, and salted. Half the water is added gradually, mixing 5 minutes, then the rest, until the paste is smooth and fairly liquid. The batter goes into banana leaves (or foil), tied tightly with string, and cooks 4 hours in the lined pot. Served hot.
ingredients: 1/2 litre water (printed; the method also uses 1 litre in the pot)
steps: Soak the beans the evening before in plenty of water. Next day rub them together to remove the white skin.
Line a thick-bottomed pot with banana leaves, central rib removed, and add 1 litre of water. Heat.
Warm the palm oil until lukewarm.
Crush the beans with the chillies. Mix with half the oil; when absorbed, add the rest and salt.
Add half the water gradually, mixing 5 minutes, then the rest. The paste should be smooth and fairly liquid.
Pour into banana leaves or foil and tie tightly with string. Cook 4 hours in the lined pot. Serve hot.
chefTips: The printed cue for the batter is ‘pâte lisse et assez liquide’ (smooth and fairly liquid).
There is no printed doneness cue; the page gives only the 4-hour time.
commonMistakes: Leaving the skins on the beans.
Adding all the water at once.
Letting the pot dry out over the 4 hours.
healthBenefits: White beans provide plant protein and fibre; palm oil adds fat.
culturalNote: The page says the dish is of Cameroonian origin from the Mbo culture and calls it the same as Nigerian moin-moin. In this printing ‘koki’ names the beans themselves.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Koki, gâteau de cornille’. Byline as printed: ‘Amina Savoura’. ‘Publié le 31 mai 2017 à 15h22’. Yield not printed (servings 6; prep 20 min are placeholders). TWO-PASS.

As printed, not reconciled: ½ litre water in the list vs 1 litre in the method (the 1 litre fills the steaming pot; the batter itself takes ½ litre across two additions). ABSENT: salt quantity; a doneness cue.
